text:
maria-g: Quick heads-up — just pushed a canary for the "redundant-kv-merge" change to runtime. Short summary: p50 latency down ~18% on short-seq workloads, overall token compute down ~11% (measured on internal tracebench with llama-13b/mistral mixes). No p99 regressions observed in the first 6h of canary.
ajohnson: Nice! What's the user-visible impact? Any change to cache hit rates or evict churn we should watch for?
maria-g: User-visible: snappier median responses for interactive flows — especially on repeated prompts with overlapping prefixes. Cache hit rate increased slightly (~3pp) because we dedupe duplicate KV entries across near-identical sessions. Evict churn decreased which reduced microbatch flushes.
slee: How is this gated? Is there a runtime flag? Will this affect Dedicated nodes or just hosted for now?
maria-g: Canary is rolled to 5% of hosted inference pods by default. There's a runtime flag to flip: runtime.features.redundant_kv_merge = true. We will not flip for Dedicated without customer opt-in; there's a safe rollout plan in the doc.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary created: rollout id r-2026-07-kvmerge, targets: hosted-us-west-2, 5% pods, start: 2026-07-02T16:40Z. Monitor links: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/r-2026-07-kvmerge
perf-bot: perf-bot: Automated canary report (6h): p50 -18.4%, p90 -6.7%, p99 +0.2% (noise). Cost-per-1M-tokens estimate: -11.1%.
ajohnson: p99 +0.2% is within noise but we should keep an eye. Any change in memory footprint on small GPUs?
maria-g: Memory delta is small — peak GPU working set down ~5% on average due to fewer duplicated KV buffers. No OOMs in canary.
tanya: Please add a short blurb to the weekly product digest and a brief note for the support playbook about expected latency wins and the opt-in for Dedicated.
maria-g: Will do. Also adding a short section to the runtime changelog and docs with the flag and rollout notes. Draft link: https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/runtime/kv-merge (wip)
slee: If customers request Dedicated enablement, what validation do we run?
maria-g: We'll run a short compatibility test (10k requests across common models), validate p99 doesn't degrade beyond 1%, and run mem/cold-start sweeps. Ops checklist: monitor p50, p99, cache_hit_rate, eviction_rate, and microbatch_flush_count during the first 48h.
ajohnson: Great — do we have an A/B dashboard tile I can point folks to?
ops-bot: ops-bot: Dashboard created: Runtime / KV Merge Canary — https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-merge-canary
maria-g: TL;DR: safe win for median latency + cost; canary live 5% hosted, Dedicated opt-in. I'll post a short summary in #product and later update the release notes. Ping me if you see any anomalies. :eyes: :party:
